steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; drain.

While the pasta water is boiling, in a large skillet over medium heat, briefly saute garlic in oil. Stir in tomatoes and their juice and sprinkle with salt. When tomatoes are bubbly, mash slightly with a fork. Stir in parsley, reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes more.
Toss hot pasta with tomato sauce, Cajun seasoning, mozzarella and Parmesan.

review.reviewBody: This was a fantastically fresh alternative to ordinary pasta sauce. I added some extra veggies (zucchini, spinach and mushrooms) and it made a tasty primavera. Bravo!

Previous reviewers were right - it is all about the creole seasoning you choose. 
I was limited to options available at my local supermarket so I went with Zatarain's. I made this for a potluck and needed to double it. After reviewing most of the reviews, I used four cans of petite diced tomatoes with no salt, fresh ground salt and pepper, basil instead of parsley, half an onion and a small jalapeño. I sautéed the onion, pepper and garlic then added the tomatoes. I seasoned that mixture with creole seasknjng before mixing one pound of bow tie pasta (agreed with the reviews that said they would decrease pasta amount) . I only used Parmesan cheese but plan to offer mozzarella cheese at the potluck.

I had to restrain myself from eating too much of this tonight. Yeah, it was that good. I sauteed some sweet mini peppers before adding the garlic and tomatoes just for a little more interest and complexity. The Cajun seasoning I used was Coleen Deon's "Cajun Spice Mix," also from this site, and I was very pleased with it. In addition to the olive oil I added butter as well, which made this silky and rich. Loved the addition of the two cheeses, but don't be tempted to add too much mozzarella or you'll risk making this stringy.

Even though I made a few mods and mine should be called "Cajun Pasta CANNA", I'm still reviewing this cause it shows how versatile it is. I had a box of whole wheat penne I wanted to use, so I used that in place of vermicelli. I did not have any fresh tomatoes, so I subbed 2 14.5 oz cans of diced. I added a couple of slices of onion, diced to the EVOO/garlic. I also added some pre-grilled/shredded chicken that had been marinated in Cajun Chicken marinade (from here on AR). I actually measured the cheeses (and used slightly less) to keep the calorie count down and this was a great weeknight meal. It's nothing I'd serve company, but we WILL eat this again. Next time, I think I'll add some spinach to get some veggies.

I used two (15 oz) cans of petit diced tomatoes with sweet onions, thin spaghetti, dried parsley, and shrimp in place of some ingredients. It turned out wonderful! Flavor was amazing and the heat was just right. I also used Luzianne Cajun seasoning. I cooked a whole box of noodles and we had a bunch left over. Maybe we were using too much sauce, but it's so good we couldn't help it! I mixed the Parmesan into the sauce and then sprinkled mozzarella on the top to serve.

this is so good! probably the best dish i've tried on this website. i used canned diced tomatoes and it was still amazing. i also simmered the tomato mixture for about 20 minutes to get rid of the watery consistency that comes from any diced tomatoes, simply because i dont like watery/liquidy pasta dishes. delicious!

Good base recipe. My attempt turned out pretty watery - don't know why - next time I may add a tbsp of flour.
After tasting the recipe as written, I added another tbsp of Cajun seasoning -- that improved the taste considerably.

Who wants to go out to dinner when you can make something this delicious at home? I sauteed some mixed, colored peppers first, which really compliment the dish. Then I added the garlic and tomatoes, letting them cook a short while. Added fresh basil, dried parsley and some butter. The Cajun seasoning here really works, adding a nice, zippy flavor. Thanks for the great recipe, Nicole.
carmelized onions made a nice addition to this recipe. I also used fresh mozzarella as well. Be sure to freeze mozzarella for 10 mins before adding to hot pasta. It prevents it from getting "gummy"

I only had 5 romas on hand so I supplemented with some canned diced tomatoes and it was still great. I made my own cajun seasoning using a recipe on this site and made the shaker available for those who like more spice. I am a wuss when it comes to spiciness but it was tame enough for me to enjoy with the measured amount of seasoning. I used less salt and whole wheat pasta for health reasons, still yummy!

It would be absolutely delicious if it wasn't way too salty. I added 2/3 of the salt to the sauce, assuming the total amount is combined for boiling the pasta and adding to the sauce. Next time I'll reverse the proportion and add only 1/3 tbsp salt (or less) to the sauce.
This has been a favorite of mine since I found it several years ago.

This was a delicious and easy recipe! I used penne pasta and added some zucchini, squash, and a pinch of dried basil. I might bump up the Cajun seasoning next time or add some red pepper flakes since I like heat, but I wouldn't change anything else. I'm sure this dish would go great with whatever veggies you happen to have in your fridge!
So good. Added more tomatoes to use up what I had and added shrimp. Will make again, for sure.
this was amazing. I just added a few more spices
Very good recipe.
I used it as a base to my pasta sauce. It was great!
Delicious! I look forward to making this again :)
This was DELICIOUS!!!! We added shrimp and bell pepper, we will be making this again FOR SURE
Made it with fresh tomatoes from our garden -- a variety of types -- so I simmered it quite a while to thicken the juices a bit. Added some fresh veggies from the garden as well. A new favorite.
